elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Garman warrants that the services provided under this Agreement, including installation, training and Maintenance Services, will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner...".

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Section 12 retained: "Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects." Specifications operate as the documentation standard for the Software.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: "for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services" — one year meets 12 months.
The inserted services warranty runs only "for a period of thirty (30) days following their performance", short of the 90-day preferred period.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted remedy sentence: "at Garman's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Software or services".
Inserted: "or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Software or services".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered operative language or the cited Section 12 text.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious code / disabling device warranty is present in the rendered language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 12 warrants conformance with the Specifications "[f]or the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date", exceeding the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted services warranty covers "installation, training and Maintenance Services ... for a period of thirty (30) days following their performance".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Sparkling's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 12 is, at Garman's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Software or services...".
"...or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Software or services."

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the retained one-year Software conformance warranty exceeds the 90-day floor, and the single inserted sentence pair supplies the missing 30-day services warranty plus an express repair/replacement-or-refund remedy tied to the Section 12 warranties.

Preferred level is not complete: the services warranty is 30 days rather than 90, and there is no compliance-with-laws warranty and no no-malicious-code warranty. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to change "thirty (30) days" to "ninety (90) days" and add express compliance-with-applicable-laws and no-malicious-code warranties.

Minimality holds: nothing outside the checklist was deleted or added — no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no procedural mechanics; the acceptance-period rejection right in Section 7/8 and the best-efforts maintenance repair mechanic in Section 10(c) are left intact.

Intent preserved: the new remedy is expressly scoped to "the warranties in this Section 12", so it does not disturb the acceptance-period "in lieu of any other remedy" rejection right (which addresses acceptance failure, a different trigger) or the fee-bearing Software Repair Services carve-out; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created.

Note for the drafter: because the acceptance-period option is stated to be "in lieu of any other remedy", consider confirming in negotiation that the new Section 12 remedy governs post-acceptance warranty breach — as drafted the two operate on distinct triggers, so no contradiction arises, but the point is worth flagging.
